newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria posts $1.7 bln trade surplus in Q1 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algeria posts $1.7 bln trade surplus in Q1 - paper.

text.p: Algeria had a trade surplus of $1.78 billion in the first quarter of 1997, the Algerian newspaper La Tribune reported on Monday.
Imports totalled $2.08 billion in the first three months of 1997 against $3.86 billion of exports in the same period, said the newspaper which gave no comparative figures for the previous period.
Algeria posted a $4.3 billion trade surplus in 1996 against a deficit of $521 million in 1995, according to government figures released last February.
The strong performance came from a nearly $1.7 billion cut in the country's import bill, a surge in international crude oil prices and a 74 percent rise in non-oil and gas exports.

The value of Algeria's exports of oil and gas, accounting for more than 90 percent of the North African country's total exports, rose to $12.5 billion in 1996, up 29 percent from 1995, according to official data.
